items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: I brought one of the many With Every Drop of Blood book you wrote with your brother Christopher... I did I think eight with my brother.

ctx.x: difficult and is interesting and is challenging and still make a living from it. And that to me has been the great blessing, that I could write and have reached the point now and have been at this point for some years where I can call my own shots. I write when I want to write and I generally manage to get paid for enough of it so that I can keep going with it.

I brought one of the many With Every Drop of Blood book you wrote with your brother Christopher. And I wonder sometimes if you’re going to write about the Civil War where does your research come from? Where do you go to try to write authentic battle scenes and those kinds of specific things?

Well the story is this. Most of my children’s books I write by myself but I did I think eight with my brother. My brother recently retired but he was an American historian at the University of Connecticut and he was the State Historian for Connecticut, a very good historian. And so we started writing together and the first book we had was called My Brother Sam is Dead and it was an enormous success, it won all the prizes and everything. And still sells a hundred thousand copies a year, which is a lot less money…
